subtopics.title: Slope Aspect — Which Side Gets the Sun

questions.question: Aspect is defined as:
options: The direction a slope faces
The steepness of a slope
The height of a valley wall
The amount of rain a slope receives

questions.question: In South Africa, north-facing slopes are the warm slopes because:
options: They are sheltered from all wind
The midday sun stands in the northern sky, so rays strike them steeply and for more hours
They are closer to the equator by hundreds of kilometres
Warm ocean currents flow past them

questions.question: Which set of features marks the SOUTH-facing wall of a Karoo valley?
options: Dry soil, sparse grass, early snowmelt
Vineyards and sun-loving fruit
Damper soil, denser green growth, snow lying longest
Bare rock with no vegetation at all

questions.question: The aspect contrast between the two walls is greatest:
options: In summer, in north-south valleys
At the equinox, in circular valleys
In spring, on windy days
In winter, in east-west valleys, when the low sun makes the angle difference extreme

subtopics.title: The Valley's Daily Breathing — Anabatic and Katabatic Winds

questions.question: The anabatic wind is:
options: The daytime upslope breeze, driven by air heating against the sunlit valley walls
The night-time downslope drainage
A regional berg wind
A sea breeze entering the valley

questions.question: The katabatic wind flows because:
options: The sun heats the valley floor
Air chilled against the radiating slopes becomes denser and slides downhill under gravity
The thermal belt pushes air upward
Fog forces air out of the valley

questions.question: Katabatic drainage is strongest on:
options: Cloudy, windy summer evenings
Hot afternoons
Clear, calm winter nights, when radiation loss is fastest
Rainy mornings

questions.question: The cumulus that crowns the peaks on summer afternoons is evidence of:
options: Katabatic drainage
Radiation fog rising
A frost pocket forming
Anabatic winds delivering warm moist air up the slopes all day

subtopics.title: Night in the Valley — Inversion, Thermal Belt, Frost and Fog

questions.question: A valley temperature inversion means that at night:
options: The coldest air lies on the valley floor with warmer air above it — temperature increases with height
The warmest air lies on the valley floor
Temperature is identical at all heights
The ridge is warmer than the free air by day

questions.question: The thermal belt is:
options: The coldest strip on the valley floor
The warm mid-slope band lying above the ponded cold air and below the chilled upper slopes
The band of cloud on the summit
The zone where the river flows

questions.question: Radiation fog forms on the valley floor when:
options: Warm rain falls into the valley
The anabatic wind lifts moisture to the ridge
The ponded moist air is cooled to its dew point and its vapour condenses
Smoke mixes with sunlight

questions.question: A dip behind a road embankment can whiten with frost while the open slope stays green because:
options: The road surface radiates cold
Embankments attract moisture
Vehicles cool the air
The hollow traps cold drainage air, forming a private frost pocket

subtopics.title: People in the Valley — Farming, Settlement and Sensible Planning

questions.question: The apple blocks of the Langkloof run along the lower-middle slopes because:
options: The thermal belt there is frost-free at night while the growing season stays long enough
The soil is deepest at that height
It is easiest to build roads there
The ridge is too windy for any crop

questions.question: Wind machines and helicopters protect orchards on critical nights by:
options: Blowing the frost off the leaves
Stirring the inversion — pulling the thermal belt's warm air down into the trees
Drying the soil
Generating heat from their engines alone

questions.question: Old farmsteads and historic valley towns typically sit on the lower slopes because that position is:
options: Closest to the river for water
The windiest and therefore coolest
Above the flood line and the worst frost, on or near the thermal belt
The cheapest land available

questions.question: Housing pushed onto cheap valley-floor land suffers because the floor is:
options: Too steep to build on
Too far from the road network
The warmest part of the valley
The coldest, foggiest, most smoke-trapped and most flood-prone zone in the landscape

subtopics.title: The Sunny Wall and the Shady Wall

questions.question: The torch trick shows that a north-facing slope is warmer because:
options: A beam striking straight on concentrates into a small bright circle, while a skimming beam smears thin
Torches shine brighter facing north
The south wall reflects all light
Light cannot reach a south-facing slope at all

questions.question: The stoep side and the pantry side of a South African east-west valley are:
options: The east and west walls
The warm north-facing wall and the cool south-facing wall
The floor and the ridge
The windward and leeward ends

questions.question: For a valley in Europe, the stoep side would face:
options: North, exactly as in South Africa
East, toward the sunrise
South, because the Northern Hemisphere midday sun stands in the southern sky
West, toward the sunset

subtopics.title: The Bathtub That Fills With Cold Air

questions.question: In the bathtub picture, the tub and the water are:
options: The valley floor and the cold katabatic air pooling on it
The ridge and the cloud on it
The river and its flood water
The thermal belt and its warm air

questions.question: The memory hook for the two valley winds is:
options: Katabatic climbs — two Ks
Anabatic ascends — two As; katabatic is gravity's wind
Both winds blow upslope
Both winds blow only in summer

questions.question: Once the tub has filled in the small hours, the temperature arrangement in the valley is:
options: Warmest at the floor, coldest above
Uniform from floor to ridge
Cold at the bottom, warmer above — the inversion, upside down from normal
Alternating warm and cold layers every few metres

questions.question: The thermal belt sits like:
options: The plug at the bottom of the tub
The tap above the basin
The water inside the tub
The rim of the tub above the waterline — the warm shelf above the cold pool

subtopics.title: Frost on the Floor, Money on the Shelf

questions.question: The two dawn hazards brewed in the valley-floor cold pool are:
options: The frost pocket and radiation fog
Thunderstorms and hail
Berg winds and drought
Floods and heat waves

questions.question: The 'money on the shelf' placement puts orchards and vineyards:
options: On the valley floor beside the river
On the thermal belt of the mid-slope, above the frost bath and below the cold heights
On the ridge crest
In the fog belt

questions.question: Roads and railways run along the valley floor because:
options: The floor never has weather hazards
The thermal belt is too warm for tar
Engineering favours flat ground — accepting the radiation-fog risk that comes with it
The slopes are all privately owned

questions.question: The physics-based fix for valley planning is:
options: All buildings on the ridge for the view
Industry on the mid-slope, houses on the floor
Everything on the valley floor for easy access
Homes on the thermal-belt shelf, smoky industry out of the inversion tub, the floor left to fields, parks and the floodplain
